verdict.rationale: Neon does publish a pricing page (neon-docs-6, neon-docs-7, neon-docs-24) with plan-level details like project counts and free-tier terms, but the evidence pack contains no actual per-unit rates for compute, storage, or traffic that would let a founder compute a bill in advance. Independent community feedback directly contradicts the predictability claim: users report confusion about the pricing basis ('What is a CPU?... pricing is based on CPU but it's never defined' — neon-comm-13) and unexpected cost jumps ('$69+ a month... It was under $10 before the switch' — neon-comm-8), and one commenter explicitly couldn't find clear pricing at all (neon-comm-5). Missing for 10: explicit published $/compute-unit, $/GB-storage, $/GB-egress rates, and resolution of the CPU-definition ambiguity that commenters flagged as undermining bill prediction.
